description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Own the data infrastructure behind an AI-powered platform for farm operations. You will build reliable ways to connect disconnected farm systems and turn their data into a consistent foundation for insights and agent-driven workflows.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build a connector framework that makes onboarding additional customers and data systems faster and more repeatable.

 - Develop AI-assisted workflows for drafting connectors from vendor documentation, then make them reliable for production use.

 - Create ways to access data from systems without APIs, including collectors that run on farm servers.

 - Design and maintain a canonical farm data model, with proposed mappings reviewed before implementation.

 - Own data quality and evaluation practices to detect and diagnose issues.

 - Build tools for agents to query data and prepare machine learning training sets, and occasionally connect systems on-site.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Two to four years of engineering experience building and operating production pipelines or integrations with messy data sources.

 - Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience using PostgreSQL, a data warehouse such as BigQuery, and tools such as dbt.

 - Experience designing schemas that other people and systems rely on, and personally troubleshooting production issues.

 - Daily experience building with AI and a practical understanding of its limitations.

 - Experience with data quality and evaluation frameworks; connector tools such as Airbyte or Fivetran are a plus.

 - Document extraction, OCR, or experience with ERP, IoT, agriculture, logistics, or food supply chain data is helpful.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary is $170,000 to $200,000 annually, plus 1% equity with four-year vesting and a one-year cliff. Healthcare and access to AI coding tools, models, and required hardware are provided. Visa sponsorship is not available; candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, California, five days a week, with about one week per quarter visiting farms in Washington, Oregon, and California.
